description: The Metal Ox in Chinese astrology: personality, Metal element traits, 1961 and 2021 dates and compatibility.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Metal Ox is the Ox born in a Metal year, one of five versions of the second animal. It combines the Ox's patience with Metal's qualities. Metal Ox years between 1924 and 2044 are 1961 and 2021. The Ox's fixed element is Earth.

sections.heading: The Metal Ox personality
paragraphs: The Metal Ox joins the sign's steady endurance to the disciplined edge of a Metal stem. Earth generates Metal in the five-element cycle, and the Ox's fixed element is Earth, so this animal is traditionally said to pour its strength into the year element, producing a person of formidable resolve. Metal Oxen are often described as principled, tireless and self-reliant, with high standards and little patience for shortcuts. They tend to be loyal, honest and protective of those under their care. Because so much energy flows outwards into Metal's determination, Metal Oxen may push themselves past sensible limits, and their certainty can harden into rigidity when they feel their principles are being challenged.

Metal is the element of autumn and harvest, and a Metal year is traditionally said to sharpen whatever animal it meets. Descriptions associate it with determination, discipline, clear judgement and a strong code of principle. Metal-year people are often portrayed as decisive, self-reliant and willing to do difficult things because they are right. The element is linked with refinement and with cutting away what is unnecessary, so it tends to bring focus and high standards. Its traditional shadow is rigidity: Metal can become inflexible, proud or emotionally guarded, preferring to be correct over being close, and finding it hard to bend once a position is taken.

sections.heading: Metal Ox at work and in love
paragraphs: At work, Metal is usually linked with discipline, precision and principled leadership. Metal-year people are often described as the ones who set standards, cut through confusion and finish what they start, which suits law, engineering, finance, surgery, editing and any role that values exactness. They tend to work well alone and lead by example. The traditional caution is inflexibility: a Metal stem can dismiss ideas that arrive untidily, so practising curiosity before judgement usually makes them better leaders.

Few combinations are pictured as more relentless at work than the Metal Ox. It sets exacting standards, follows procedure to the letter and tends to excel in auditing, heavy industry, structural engineering, compliance and senior administration. Clear lines of authority and the freedom to finish a job properly suit it, whereas constant reorganisation grates. Within a marriage or long friendship it is principled and utterly reliable, keeping every promise it makes however inconvenient. What it seeks is somebody who prizes integrity and does not need constant flattery. The weak point is severity: a Metal Ox can judge a loved one's untidy habits or emotional outbursts harshly, and compromise may feel to it like quietly lowering the bar.

sections.heading: Metal Ox years and dates
paragraphs: Metal Ox years in the Lunar New Year table run from February 15, 1961 to February 4, 1962 and from February 12, 2021 to January 31, 2022. Because the year begins at Lunar New Year, a birthday in January or early February needs checking: in 1961 anyone born before Feb 15 is a Metal Rat, not a Metal Ox. Sixty years separate each Metal Ox year, the length of a full round of five elements and twelve animals. Every Metal Ox year is Yin, matching the Ox's own polarity.

Its traditional name is Xin-Chou: Xin is the yin Metal stem and Chou is the Ox's branch. Births just before each new year fall in the Metal Rat year (before February 15, 1961) and the Metal Rat year (before February 12, 2021), and births in the weeks after each Metal Ox year ends belong to the Water Tiger. The new year itself fell on a Wednesday in 1961 and Friday in 2021.

sections.heading: Growth edges and compatibility for the Metal Ox
paragraphs: Growth for the Metal Ox usually lies in flexibility and self-care. Readings suggest that the combination can treat rest as weakness and compromise as defeat, both of which tend to wear down relationships and health over time. Making room for other people's methods, even untidy ones, often brings unexpected improvements. Metal Oxen may also find it hard to show vulnerability; letting a trusted person see doubt or fatigue builds closeness. Creative hobbies that have no measurable goal can be surprisingly restorative. When it learns that strength includes yielding, the Metal Ox becomes a principled leader whom others follow willingly.

For relationships, the classical structures belong to the animal rather than the element, so the Metal Ox shares the Ox's San He trine with the Snake and Rooster (the Metal trine), its Liu He bond with the Rat, and its Liu Chong clash with the Goat. The element adds a second layer: another Metal sign shares this year element, while partners whose year element feeds Metal in the generating cycle are often described as supportive.

faq.question: What years are Metal Ox years?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044: 1961 (from February 15, 1961) and 2021 (from February 12, 2021). Each lasts until the day before the next Lunar New Year.

faq.question: What is the Metal Ox's element relationship?
faq.answer: The year element is Metal and the Ox's fixed element is Earth; in the five-element cycles earth generates Metal. Readings use that relationship to describe how easily the two sides of the sign sit together.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Metal Ox?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Snake and Rooster (San He) and the Rat (Liu He). The Goat is the Liu Chong clash. These pairings depend on the animal, whatever the element.

faq.question: What is the Metal Ox called in the Chinese calendar?
faq.answer: Xin-Chou. In almanacs and Four Pillars charts each year is named by its heavenly stem, here the Metal stem Xin, followed by its earthly branch, here Chou for the Ox, so the name pins down both halves of the combination at once.

faq.question: How is the Metal Ox different from other Oxs?
faq.answer: All Oxs share patience, diligence and steady strength. The Metal year element changes the tone: metal is the element of autumn and harvest, and a Metal year is traditionally said to sharpen whatever animal it meets.
